body:
```
inaccessible_object_exception: Unable to make field private final java.lang.String org.apache.lucene.document.SortedNumericDocValuesRangeQuery.field accessible: module org.apache.lucene.core does not "opens org.apache.lucene.document" to module org.elasticsearch.server
```

The error is coming from code introduced by b5af845ee76e4408d9a7b6c18e725a17cce6417b last October, so it's surprising that it's only become visible now.  Has anything changed with how elasticsearch is being modularised recently?  cc @ChrisHegarty

> Has anything changed with how elasticsearch is being modularised recently?

Nothing has changed about how server is modularized. I'm skeptical this code actually worked, is it possible it wasn't actually exercised outside of unit tests? Unit tests run non-modular, so we wouldn't hit this unless running integration tests or in a real scenario, and I only see unit tests in the linked commit.

Can we avoid using setAccessible? If we need access to these fields, why can't we make them accessible in Lucene?

As it stands, for this to work, we need to open the `org.apache.lucene.document` package. We do similar elsewhere, but as a stopgap until the Lucene fields or APIs can be updated. See https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/e7a4eecc3ab7cd8e54f0e0027a6fd3331028e69f/distribution/tools/server-cli/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/server/cli/SystemJvmOptions.java#L64-L65

> is it possible it wasn't actually exercised outside of unit tests?

Very plausibly!

> If we need access to these fields, why can't we make them accessible in Lucene?

It's slightly tricky as there are a whole bunch of package-private classes involved here, but I think we can cover this with a public interface implemented by the classes in question.  I'll open an issue.

> as a stopgap until the Lucene fields or APIs can be updated

Thanks Chris, that should fix things in the immediate term.
Thinking about this more, given that a) it looks like it has never worked in production code and b) we haven't seen any regressions because of it, I think it's safe to just remove this code.
